# CI Workflows

- `reusable-consumer.yml`: nine checks plus the `dx-ci (aggregate)` gate.
- `reusable-release.yml`: on a tag push, or on any ref when `publish` is false, dry-runs on each `platforms` entry, then applies `dx deploy` for each `deployment` tagged `release` (or the `deployables` input), the `registry_deploys` of a `github_deploy` first, with `contents`, `id-token`, `attestations` and `packages` write. The release job runs only when `publish` is true (the default) and the ref is a tag, so a branch run never publishes. A failure stops the rest and the job summary lists what was published. `dx init` writes a `release.yml` caller.
- `release-e2e.yml`: on a `v0.0.0-e2e.*` tag push, calls `reusable-release.yml` from this repository with the `//tools/testing/release_e2e` fixtures: `a_github` alone, or `a_github` then `b_refuses` when the tag contains `partial`. `b_refuses` keeps the placeholder tag `v0.0.0-dryrun`, so its dry run passes and its publish fails.
- `reusable-docs.yml`: `docs-check` plus `docs-publish` (GitHub Pages).
- `docs.yml`: on a push to `main` that changes a page in the user book (`docs/`, `tools/docs/`, the root and example READMEs), runs `reusable-docs.yml` and publishes the book to https://devhusdk.github.io/rules_dx/. Runs share the `docs-pages-<ref>` concurrency group, so two Pages deploys never overlap.
- `ci.yml`: on pull requests and in the merge queue, first runs the `changes` job, which lists the changed files. When every one is a `.md` file outside `tests/`, `testdata/`, `fixtures/`, `fixture/` and `demo/` directories, the change is docs only and the `check` jobs skip. Otherwise it runs `dx check --affected` as the jobs `check (<platform>)` on `linux_x86_64`, `linux_arm64`, `macos_arm64`, `windows_x86_64` and `windows_arm64`. `check (linux_x86_64)` runs `dx check --affected --coverage --report lcov=$RUNNER_TEMP/coverage/lcov.info` instead, which runs each affected test once: under coverage when it can take coverage, else in the plain test phase. It uploads the report as `coverage-linux_x86_64` for 7 days. No other platform measures coverage. On pull requests `dx check` skips the tests tagged `network-consumer` or `audit` (the gate's `pr_tags`), which `audit.yml` runs. Each job uploads the dx JSON output as `check-<platform>` for 7 days. The gate sets `DX_PROFILE_DIR`, so each Bazel call inside `dx check` writes a profile, and uploads them as `profiles-check-<platform>` for 7 days. The jobs use `.github/actions/gate`, which pins the base with `gate_base`: the pull request base, or the queue base in the merge queue. The gate builds `gate_base`, dx and `producers_bin` in one `bazel build` and runs copies outside `bazel-bin`, because the Bazel runs inside dx can rebuild dx and Windows cannot replace a running exe. `check (linux_x86_64)` also runs `dx generate` on the whole repo, except on a pull request. In the merge queue, the `changes` job fails when an `evidence/*` status on the pull request head is not green. Run the same locally with `tools/dx check --affected`. The `check` jobs never run on dispatch, because `dogfood` already checks `//...` on every platform. Every other job runs only on dispatch. The `ci` job is the one required check: on pull requests and in the merge queue it needs `changes` and, unless the change is docs only, every `check` job; on dispatch it needs every dispatch job. A failed Windows preflight build uploads `rmeta-diagnostics-<platform>`.
- When the `evidence.yml` test task fails, `producers_bin --test-log-tails` prints the last 80 lines of each failing test's `test.log` in its own `::group::` in the job log, for the first 20 failing tests.
- `ci.yml` job `in-graph-prebuilt-guard` runs `//tools/testing/consumer:in_graph_prebuilt_guard`, which analyzes the `IN_GRAPH_GUARD_LANGS` consumer fixtures of `@dx_api_fixtures` on linux_x86_64, and the `MACOS_IN_GRAPH_GUARD_LANGS` and `WINDOWS_IN_GRAPH_GUARD_LANGS` ones with `--langs` on macos_arm64 and windows_x86_64, with `--//cli/prebuilt:guard_view` and the `dx check` and `dx docs` aspects and fails when they compile a rules_dx binary that `tools/testing/consumer/prebuilt_guard_allowlist.txt` does not name.
- `ci.yml` job `analysis-scaling` runs `//tools/testing:analysis_scaling_check`, which analyzes the `//tools/testing/deep_graph` chains of depth 100 and 400 with the `dx check`, `dx docs` and `dx sync` aspects and fails when depth 400 takes more than 8 or less than 2 times depth 100.
- `audit.yml`: the only workflow with a schedule, daily at `17 3 * * *` UTC, and by dispatch. No job retries a test. Its jobs:
  - `network`: the tests tagged `network-consumer`.
  - `quickstart`: the README quickstart case of `//deploy/private/release/tests:release_consumer_smoke_test` with the network on (`DX_NESTED_BAZEL_NETWORK=1`) and no cached result.
  - `hermetic`, `hermetic-macos` and `hermetic-windows`: the clean-machine consumer qualifications, with no installs and the network denied, on `linux_x86_64`, `macos_arm64`, `windows_x86_64` and `windows_arm64`. Each uploads `hermetic-evidence-<platform>`.
  - `determinism`: seven shards. Each builds a seventh of the top-level packages that hold one target of each `lang.json` entry_points kind, plus `//appimage/...` (shard 0), `//cli/archive/...` (shard 1), `//android/private/packaging/...` (shard 2), `//msix/tests/...` (shard 3), `//deploy/private:all` (shard 5) or the rest of `//deploy/private/...` (shard 6), twice in fresh output bases with no cache and compares the execution logs against `tools/ci/determinism_allowlist.txt`.
  - `msix-install`: `//msix/tests:install_test` on `windows_x86_64`, which installs the signed and unsigned packages and launches the app.
  - `verify-pins`: `//core/quality/artifacts:update -- --verify-only`. It fails naming each stale record.
  - `license-terms`: hashes the terms in `core/licenses/pins.json` and opens, or comments on, the issue "licenses: terms changed upstream" when they changed.
  - `patch-upstream`: `//patches:upstream`. It reads the `Upstream:` header of each patch under `patches/` and the `# Upstream:` carry markers in `BUILD` and `.bzl` files, and opens, or updates, the issue "patches: upstream fixes released" when an upstream pull request is merged and in a release, a ref was closed without a merge, or a patch has no header.
  - `upgrade-e2e`: `producers_bin --upgrade-e2e`. A throwaway consumer on the second-latest BCR release runs `dx init`, upgrades to the latest and back with `dx upgrade --to <version> --apply`, and runs `bazel test //...` after each step. It passes without a run while the BCR lists fewer than two releases. `producers_bin --upgrade-e2e --from <from> --to local` upgrades to this checkout instead (`local_path_override` at the root `MODULE.bazel` version), so the run uses the tree's own dx. After `dx init` and each upgrade it reads `bazel mod graph --output=json` and fails when the consumer names `rules_php`, `rules_lua` or `rules_qt`, when a rule set does not resolve to exactly the floor of the target rules_dx release, or when rules_dx does not resolve to the target version.
  - `unlabelled-issues`: warns about open issues older than one day, except pinned ones, that have no P0 to P3 label, and lists them in the job summary.
  - `missing-labels`: warns about labels named in `CONTRIBUTING.md` or issue template front matter that do not exist in the repository.
  - `blocked-issues`: removes the `blocked` label once every blocker named on the `Blocked on:` line is done, and comments once on a `blocked` issue without the line.
  - `unreviewed-merges`: warns about, and comments once on, pull requests merged in the last two days that touched `.github/review-paths.txt` paths without a `Review:` comment.
  - `dispatch`: on `main`, dispatches `ci.yml` and `advisory-publish.yml` every day and `dx-update.yml` on Mondays.
  - `report`: on `main`, after every other job, rewrites the pinned issue labelled `known-red` with the failed jobs and the test labels that failed in the run, and opens it when none is open.
- `evidence.yml`: native evidence on hosted runners, dispatched per run. The run posts the commit status `evidence/<platform>/<task>/<scope>` on the dispatched commit: pending at dispatch, then success, failure or error. The `evidence-<platform>` artifact holds `evidence.log` and each test's log, XML and undeclared outputs. Set `platforms` to `["macos_arm64"]` for Apple runs. Set `android` to boot an emulator and run the Rust Android device scenarios on `linux_x86_64`. Set `qualify` on `windows_x86_64` to run `//cc/private/tools/context:qualify` for llvm and msvc. Set `relocate` (test or build). With `task=test` it reruns the task under a fresh `--output_base` with the disk cache off and remote cache hits refused; the second run logs to `relocated.log`, and `bazel-testlogs` then points at the relocated base. With `task=build` it runs `//tools/testing:determinism_check` on `scope`, which builds it twice in fresh output bases with no cache and compares the execution logs against `tools/ci/determinism_allowlist.txt`; its output is `determinism.txt` and it fails on any unlisted difference. Set `lock_refresh` to regenerate `MODULE.bazel.lock` on the platform before the scope task and fail when it differs from the checkout; the refreshed lock and `lock.diff` land in `lock/` of the artifact, so a lock entry that only changes on Windows can be copied back. Set `release_cell` to build and qualify the platform's release cell first with `producers_bin --release-cell`, the command `release-cells.yml` runs, uncached and without RBE; the files land in `release-cell/` of the artifact. A Windows release cell needs `accept_licenses` set to the ids that `windows_accept_licenses` of `release-cells.yml` defaults to. The job allows 60 minutes, 90 with `release_cell`, and 180 with `release_cell` on `windows_x86_64` and `windows_arm64`, as `release-cells.yml` does.
- `cancel-on-close.yml`: when a pull request closes or merges, cancels every queued or running run on its head branch, of any workflow but itself. A newer close of the same pull request cancels an older run of it. It skips pull requests from forks and from the default branch.
- `comment-command.yml`: runs the slash commands of issue and pull request comments from owners, members and collaborators. Each command is its own job, filtered on the first line of the comment, so a comment without a command starts no job.
  - `/evidence`: a comment on an issue or pull request whose first line starts with `/evidence` dispatches `evidence.yml` and replies with the run URL. On a pull request it runs on the PR branch, otherwise on `main`. Arguments are `platforms=`, `task=`, `scope=`, `test_timeout=`, `displays=`, `android=`, `qualify=`, `relocate=`, `release_cell=`, `flags=`, `lock_refresh=` and `accept_licenses=`, for example `/evidence platforms=["macos_arm64"] task=test scope=//haskell/...`. `evidence.yml` validates them and a rejected run fails there.
  - `/lock-refresh`: a comment on a pull request whose first line is `/lock-refresh` dispatches `lock-refresh.yml` on the PR branch with `pr` set to that pull request and replies with the run URL. The only argument is `nested=true` or `nested=false` (the default). A pull request from a fork is rejected.
- `dx-update.yml`: `tools/dx update --pr` for dependency updates, dispatched by `audit.yml` on Mondays or by hand. `dx init` writes `cli/adopt/templates/dx-update.yml`, the same workflow without the BuildBuddy remote execution steps. Where `lock-refresh.yml` exists, it then dispatches that workflow for each open `dx-update/` branch whose `MODULE.bazel.lock` changes the `rules_python` `python` or `rules_go` `go_sdk` entries.
- `lock-refresh.yml`: dispatch-only. Runs `bazel mod deps --lockfile_mode=update` on the five platforms, merges them with `producers_bin --lock-merge`, which starts from the `linux_x86_64` lock and replaces each extension's `os:<os>,arch:<arch>` entry whole with the one from that platform's own lock (and deep-merges `facts`); it fails when a platform lock is missing, a directory is not a known platform, or an extension has a key other than `general` or a platform factor, normalises the result with Bazel and uploads the locks as an artifact to commit. Run it with `--ref <branch>` after changing `MODULE.bazel` when an extension is locked per platform; one host only writes its own entries. With `nested` set, it also runs the nested tests in record mode on `linux_x86_64`, `linux_arm64`, `macos_arm64`, `windows_x86_64` and `windows_arm64` and merges their records into `tools/testing/nested_cache` with `nested_cache_update --from`; dispatch it that way after a `bazel_dep` bump. With `android_maven` set, it also runs `REPIN=1 bazel run @rules_android_maven//:pin` on `ubuntu-latest`, so the lock is not resolved through Coursier on a throttled network, and adds `third_party/jvm/rules_android_maven_install.json` to the artifact; dispatch it that way after a rules_android or rules_flutter bump. With `crates` set, its merge job also repins the `@crates`, `@dx_quality_crates` and `@dx_thrift_crates` hubs with `CARGO_BAZEL_REPIN=workspace` and adds the `cargo-bazel-lock.json` files to the artifact; dispatch it that way after changing a crate annotation. With the `pr` input, the merge job also commits the merged locks, nested cache sets, android maven pin and crate pins to that pull request's branch, using the dx-update app token, and does nothing when they are unchanged.
- `release-cells.yml`: reusable, read-only. Builds, independently rebuilds and qualifies one archive per `//deploy/private/release:release_matrix` cell on its native runner (a consumer Bazel build included), then verifies all records. The `windows_accept_licenses` input (by default the Visual Studio Build Tools licence) lists the licence ids the Windows cells' consumers accept at `dx init`; it is the only place the release names a licence. Artifacts: `release-cell-<name>` per cell and the combined `release-cells`; outputs: `version`, `sha`, `workflow_ref`. It fails when any cell is rejected, and a rejected cell never stops the others. Each matrix row sets its own job timeout: 180 minutes for the Windows cells, 90 for the others.
- `release-tools.yml`: reusable, read-only. Builds the deadnix, selene, topiary and progenitor binaries on `linux-x86_64`, `linux-arm64`, `macos-arm64`, `windows-x86_64` and `windows-arm64` (static musl binaries on Linux), ad-hoc signs the `macos-arm64` ones, builds static kcov on the two Linux hosts as `dx-kcov-<host>`, builds it a second time and compares the two execution logs with `//tools/testing:determinism_check`, and uploads `release-tool-<host>`, holding the binaries, their licences, the deadnix source crate and the kcov source archive. Its `python-tools` job builds one `dx-<tool>-<host>.tar.gz` archive per core Python quality tool and release host on `linux-x86_64` and uploads `release-tool-python-tools`. Its `go` job cross-builds the `dx-go-<host>` Go tool multicall, `dx-oapi-codegen-<host>` and `dx-gopackagesdriver-<host>` for every release host on `linux-x86_64`, checks each binary's format, copies `dx-oapi-codegen-LICENSE` and `dx-gopackagesdriver-LICENSE`, runs the Linux ones and uploads `release-tool-go`. Its `python-tools`, `go`, `jars` and `haskell` jobs, its `hackage` job except the `macos-arm64` hlint leg, and every leg of its `tools` job, also build their assets twice in fresh output bases with `//tools/testing:determinism_check` and fail when the execution logs differ.
- `release.yml`: calls `release-cells.yml` for the five platform archives and `release-tools.yml` for the tool binaries, builds the `rules_dx-<version>.tar.gz` source archive (after `release_driver` checks the tag against the candidate commit), then attests the manifest and uploads them through `release_driver` with the raw dx and dx gazelle binaries, `.sha256` files, the `dx-sha256sums.txt` and `dx-gazelle-sha256sums.txt` and `dx-tool-sha256sums.txt` manifests, and `source.json` to the release, then runs `dx security --verify` on `dx-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` and the source archive and on a one-byte-modified copy of each. The `dry_run` dispatch input runs the same `source`, `attest` and `assets` chain on the cells' version, skips every step that needs a pushed tag, signing or publishing, and still checks the `release-assets` paths. No asset is ever replaced once uploaded: a rerun skips identical assets and fails on a different one.
- `release-consumer.yml`: runs when a release is published, or by dispatch with a `tag`. On the five release platforms it checks the platform archive and the source archive with `gh attestation verify` against the published bundles, resolves `rules_dx` through the BCR when it lists the version and otherwise through a local registry made from the published `source.json`, builds the quickstart consumer with no override, and checks that `@rules_dx//dx/launch:dx` is the prebuilt download and prints the released version, that topiary and progenitor are the prebuilt downloads, that `@rules_dx//config:tool_govet` is the prebuilt dx-go and `tool_modfmt` runs, on Linux that kcov is the prebuilt download, and on `windows-arm64` that the `pkl_lsp` natives jar packs the prebuilt tree-sitter and tree-sitter-pkl DLLs. It skips releases whose tag does not start with `v`, such as `mirror-php-<version>`. When every `consumer` job is green, its `bcr` job calls `bazel-contrib/publish-to-bcr` (pinned v1.7.0) to open the BCR pull request from the `BCR_REGISTRY_FORK` fork with `BCR_PUBLISH_TOKEN`; it is skipped while that variable is unset and for `v0.0.*` tags. Its `bcr-ledger` job runs `//deploy/private/release:bcr_ledger` and records the pull request URL, `failed`, or `not-authorized` for a skipped `bcr` job, in the run summary and the `bcr-ledger` artifact.

## Main health

`audit.yml` runs daily against the default branch head. After each run on main, its `report` job rewrites the pinned issue labelled `known-red` with the test labels that failed in that run. GitHub may delay or drop scheduled runs under load.

`ci.yml` runs every job but `changes` and `check` on `workflow_dispatch`. Pull requests and the merge queue run only `changes`, the `check` jobs and `ci`. A push to `main` runs nothing. The `audit` workflow dispatches `ci.yml` on `main` once a day. Runs share one concurrency group per ref (`ci-ci-<ref>`, and `ci-ci-main-refs/heads/main` for dispatches): a new push cancels the older pull request run, and a new dispatch on main replaces only the queued one. Closing or merging a pull request starts a `ci` run in its group, which cancels the queued or running one; all its jobs skip. `cancel-on-close.yml` then cancels the other runs on the branch.

The platform table is `PLATFORMS` in `tools/ci/input_validation/src/lib.rs`; `input_validation_test` pins every other copy to it.

Land a PR with `gh pr merge <n> --squash --auto`. It joins the merge queue, which squash-merges up to five pull requests at a time once `ci` passes on the queued commit. Never use `--admin`.

`.github/rulesets/main.json` requires one check on main: `ci`.

The consumer contract is [GitHub CI](../../docs/github-ci.md).
